why: The THEMES of the dungeon room kit (tools/dungeon_rooms.py, tools/dungeon_kinds.py, docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_ROOMS.md): the blocks a dungeon's rooms are drawn in and the dressing rules that make a room look like what it is. A dungeon names one in data/dungeons.json (dungeons[].theme). Vanilla blocks only (the pocket is a void dimension: nothing here is checked against the overworld's spawn blocks).
rules: Every block of the hull (wall, floor, ceiling) is OPAQUE. The pocket has skylight at a fixed noon (data/portals.json pocket.generator), so a leaf or glass hull would let daylight into every room; leaves are interior dressing only.
No block that falls (sand, gravel, anvil) and no concrete anywhere (contract C4). No hazard (lava, fire, magma, cactus, berry bush, cobweb, campfire, powder snow, pointed dripstone).

Nothing in the hull or the dressing is on the rift pick's can_break list: the decorative 'ores' of a wall are raw blocks and coal blocks, never ore. The seam's ores sit in a 3-thick slab of unbreakable rock (kind resources), so mining one opens a pocket, never a hole to the void.
Water exists only one block deep, at floor level, over a bed (a deeper pool would need walls under the floor course and would flow into the void).

A dress spec with "lit": true emits light and is skipped in a dark_room. A spec with "level": "full" places obstacles (trunks, columns, piles) and only runs in rooms whose kind is dressed 'full', off a trail kept clear for the player.

desert_excavation.why: OVERWORLD2 (2026-10-11), the Zero Dig: an archaeological excavation in a desert. Cut sandstone walls and smooth sandstone floors in terraced trenches, red-sand strata (orange, yellow, red and brown terracotta) in the walls, the carved stonework of a buried city (chiseled and cut red sandstone) showing in them, oak scaffolds and hanging work lamps, spoil heaps of coarse dirt, standing and fallen buried columns. No gravity block anywhere a player walks or can mine: the kit refuses sand, red sand, gravel and suspicious sand, so the whole dig is cut and smooth stone, terracotta and dirt. Plain sandstone (and its stairs, slabs and wall, whose ids start with it) is deliberately absent: it is the flooded ruin fossil-bay dig block and the extras tests require no theme to name it; this theme uses the dig block of its own fossil bay (data/dungeon_extras2.json fossils.dig).

life.why: A dig in the dunes: sand burrowers in the spoil, cactus and scorpions in the shade, ancient clay figures that woke, scavengers and a few bones of whatever the city kept. The dressing is the expedition that dug too deep: a field camp, a trench collapse, a skeleton half uncovered, a stele with candles, crates, waxed field notes.

night_crater.name: The crater
night_crater.why: OVERWORLD2 (2026-10-11), the Starfall Crater: a meteor crater under a night sky. Blackstone walls and a floor of tuff under an obsidian sky pricked with pearlescent froglight stars, crying obsidian dripping its purple light, amethyst seams and crystal spires, fallen meteor iron, smooth basalt and polished tuff rubble. Deep rock, so the seam is deepslate ore (glowing in its vein). No budding amethyst (it grows clusters at random), no regular ore as decoration (only the seam is ore).

tall_lights.why: a deep crater hall is lit from below by starlight that fell into the floor: pearlescent froglight set into the tuff every 9

shapes.why: OVERWORLD2: a crater is round: bowls (oval), a central plug of fallen rock (ring, rock), a broken rim (split: terraces), shattered rock (cavern), the curve of the rim (gallery)
shapes.secret_block_why: a seamed slab of the crater wall where the rock cracked under the strike; in no other hull or dressing of the theme

life.why: The crater is a place the night keeps: moon creatures that came to see, sleepers in the bowl, stones that fell and woke, small lights, watchers. The dressing is an observatory that came to study the strike: a night camp, a rock fall, a skeleton under a blanket of dust, a shrine of purple candles, waxed star charts.
